title: Orbit Fare Machine
one_liner: Slide propellant cost, fuel share and payload to see the price per kilogram and your own ticket to orbit.
speaker: Peter Diamandis
context: After the Starship tower catch, Peter reasoned that if fuel is about a quarter of operating cost, flights cost a few million dollars, or tens of dollars per kilogram. He compared that with the Shuttle, and later used Elon's lower fuel figure to get tickets under $1,000.
demo: Visitors drag sliders for propellant cost per flight, fuel's share of operating cost and payload tons, and enter their body weight. A live readout shows cost per flight, cost per kg and their personal ticket price. A log-scale bar chart compares that with the Shuttle figure, and preset buttons load Peter's case and Elon's updated case.
data_plan: A bundled set of figures stated on the podcast (propellant cost, 25% fuel share, Shuttle $/kg, Elon's $500,000 and 200-ton update); every other value comes from user sliders, clearly labelled as user assumptions.
risks: Peter's own range implies a payload of roughly 150 tons that was never stated, so the 'Peter case' preset must not invent a payload; instead it should show the stated $/kg outputs. The fuel-share rule of thumb is a heuristic, not a SpaceX figure. Body weight is personal but stays local.
